data.content_ref: inline:The claim explicitly states the preference is for the theory 'subjected to the most rigorous scrutiny, regardless of outcome,' removing outcome as a factor. But the mechanism immediately reintroduces outcome as a factor, saying we focus resources on 'the theory that has survived the hardest tests.' 'Survived' is an outcome. If outcome is genuinely irrelevant ('regardless of outcome'), then a theory subjected to the most rigorous scrutiny but which failed those tests should be equally preferred. The mechanism's own formulation ('has survived') contradicts the claim's 'regardless of outcome,' smuggling the very outcome-dependence the claim was supposed to dissolve. This makes the proposed dissolution self-undermining: either the claim is wrong (outcome matters, as the mechanism admits) or the mechanism is wrong (we prefer scrutiny-severity alone, in which case failed theories are equally preferable). The target cannot have both.
